# Dynamic Peeps

**Status:** specification (not yet implemented)
**Milestone:** 4 candidate — builds on Milestone 3 behavior scripts

Dynamic peeps are NPCs whose behavior script and dialog tree are periodically
**regenerated by an LLM agent** from two inputs:

1. their currently active behavior artifact, and
2. a durable log of interactions observed since the last behavior update.

The agent runs **out of process** against a DB-backed job queue. Its output is
**validated** (referential integrity, additive-only rules, size budget) and
**layered over** the hand-authored behavior, which is an immutable floor. A
generation failure never degrades gameplay: the worst case is a static peep.

> [!WARNING]
> Dynamic peeps execute **agent-generated Python in-process**. This is gated
> behind a dev-only feature flag and is **not safe for production**. See
> [§9 Safety posture](#9-safety-posture) for the mandatory guardrails and the
> blocking v1.1 hardening gate.

## 1. Scope and locked decisions

| Area | Decision | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execution model | Agent-generated Python, **trusted**, dev-only feature flag | Highest risk. No sandbox in v1; see [§9](#9-safety-posture) |
| Mobility | **Room-bound** | No NPC position schema, no attachment re-registration, no NPC presence events. Removes ~30% of the work |
| Authorship | **Layered overlay**; authored floor invoked first, never modified | A bad generation cycle can never make a peep unusable |
| Agent placement | **Out-of-process worker**, DB-backed leased job queue | The game event loop never blocks on a model call |
| Dialog mutation | **Append-only**, `dynamic_`-prefixed, cycle-scoped node ids | No authored `action_id` can be re-issued or voided |
| Observation log | New `peep_observations` table plus a rolled-up digest | Net-new schema; the agent reads digests, never raw rows |
| Artifact storage | `.local/peep-overlays/<peep_id>/v<version>.py`, one immutable file per version | Versions are diffable and roll-backable; forces a distinct import path |
| Cadence | `dynamic: {cadence: daily\|hourly}` in `peeps.yaml`, default `daily`; hourly is opt-in | Cheapest useful default; expressive peeps can opt in |
| Cost ceiling | Fixed conservative default: **2 calls / peep / game-day**, **40k tokens / peep / game-day**, plus a global daily ceiling | Overridable via `TRSERVER_*` |
| Size budget | **Logical lines** (non-blank, non-comment): behavior ≤ 500, overlay-authored ≤ 150 | Mirrors the repo's existing 1200-line static rule |

### 1.1 Why room-bound matters

`doc/design.md` already constrains peeps to room granularity — peeps have no
position on the board. The existing runtime bakes each NPC into exactly one
room at load time (`server/behaviors/loader.py:125-134`), and `PeepDefinition`
is a frozen dataclass whose `room_id` is a literal string with no persistence
behind it. Supporting movement would require a world-state schema change, a
dispatcher routing change, and NPC presence broadcasting. v1 deliberately
avoids all of that, and R5.6 asserts the invariant with a test.

---

## 2. Definitions

- **Authored floor** — the `peeps.yaml` entry and its `peeps/<name>.py` script
  as committed in the world content tree. Immutable at runtime.
- **Overlay artifact** — a versioned, agent-generated Python module that
  extends the authored floor. It never edits the floor.
- **Behavior version** — a monotonically increasing integer per peep,
  incremented on each successful overlay commit. The runtime always loads the
  highest `active` version.
- **Observation** — a single durable record of one peep-directed interaction.
- **Observation window** — the interval between two behavior updates: one game
  day or one hour. The agent reads the current window plus the previous
  version's artifact, and nothing else.
- **Digest** — a bounded, pre-aggregated summary of one window's observations.
  This is the only observation input the agent receives.
- **Dynamic peep** — an authored NPC declared `dynamic` in `peeps.yaml` that has
  at least one committed behavior version.

---

## 3. Requirements

### R1 — Observation capture

- **R1.1** Every interaction directed at a peep MUST be recorded as an
  observation, durably, within the same transaction that applies its effect.
  Losing an observation is a correctness bug, not a degradation.
- **R1.2** The captured vocabulary MUST be the existing `BehaviorEvent`
  vocabulary — `quick_action`, `card_play`, `dialog_action`, `activity_result`,
  `enter`, `leave`. This milestone introduces no new runtime event types.
- **R1.3** Each observation MUST record the **subject** (the peep observed), the
  **actor** (`kind` of `user` | `npc` | `system`, plus account or peer id),
  `room_id`, `event_type`, `action`, and a bounded `detail_json`.
- **R1.4** `detail_json` MUST be schema-versioned and MUST NOT contain raw chat
  text, credentials, session tokens, or password material. Any retained free
  text MUST be length-capped and stored separately from structured fields.
- **R1.5** Capture MUST NOT change the semantics, ordering, or transactional
  boundaries of the existing dispatch path. It is an additive write alongside
  an already-committed intent application.
- **R1.6** `activity_result` observations SHOULD be emitted. The activity bridge
  (`server/routes/activity_bridge.py:17-44`) currently does not dispatch this
  event; closing that gap is in scope because it is the highest-signal
  observation type.
- **R1.7** Observations MUST be attributed to the behavior version live at
  capture time, so a version's quality can be evaluated against what it saw.

### R2 — Digest and retention

- **R2.1** A digest MUST be produced per peep per window **before** the agent is
  invoked. The agent MUST NOT read raw observation rows.
- **R2.2** The digest MUST be **bounded and deterministic**: counts per
  `(event_type, action)`, distinct-actor counts, per-actor interaction tallies
  (top-N by count, remainder summarized), and a chronological list of up to K
  recent safe summaries.
- **R2.3** The digest MUST include a `per_user` section keyed by account id for
  actors the peep interacted with at least twice in the window, so the agent can
  form durable per-user memory. Single-interaction strangers are aggregated,
  not enumerated.
- **R2.4** Raw observations MUST be pruned on a rolling retention window
  (default 7 game-days). Digests MUST be retained longer (default 30 game-days)
  because they are cheap and support audit.
- **R2.5** Pruning MUST be batched and MUST NOT run on the event path.

### R3 — Agent pipeline

- **R3.1** Generation MUST be triggered by a cadence scheduler, never by
  gameplay events. Supported cadences: `daily`, aligned to the
  `TRSERVER_TIMEZONE` game-day boundary via `server/game_time.py`; and
  `hourly`. Cadence is per peep and defaults to daily.
- **R3.2** The scheduler MUST enqueue a job row. It MUST NOT perform the model
  call.
- **R3.3** The worker MUST process jobs out of process, over an outbound HTTPS
  client modelled on `server/mc_client.py`. It MUST NOT share the game server's
  event loop.
- **R3.4** A job MUST be idempotent per `(peep, window)`: enqueuing a duplicate
  MUST NOT produce a second artifact for the same window.
- **R3.5** Jobs MUST be leased with expiry, so a crashed worker's jobs are
  reclaimed rather than lost. Expired-lease recovery MUST be bounded and logged.
- **R3.6** The worker MUST enforce per-cycle wall-clock and token budgets and
  MUST abort a generation that exceeds them, leaving the previous artifact live.
- **R3.7** The worker MUST enforce a per-peep daily call and token cap
  (defaults 2 calls and 40k tokens per peep per game-day, plus a global daily
  ceiling) to bound cost and prevent rewrite loops.
- **R3.8** Every job MUST terminate in exactly one state: `succeeded`,
  `rejected` (validation failure), `skipped` (budget, cap, or empty window), or
  `failed` (transport or parse error). State and reason MUST be persisted.
- **R3.9** Provider credentials MUST come from environment configuration, MUST
  never be persisted to the world DB, and MUST never appear in logs or
  artifacts.
- **R3.10** The worker MUST refuse to start when the feature flag is off, and
  the world server MUST behave exactly as it does today in that case.

### R4 — Artifact validation and budget

No generated artifact reaches the runtime until it passes all of the following.
Validation failures are terminal and leave the prior version live.

- **R4.1** The validator MUST be a pure function of `(artifact, world snapshot)`
  so it is unit-testable without a model or a network.
- **R4.2** **Parse.** The artifact must parse as Python.
- **R4.3** **Budget.** Behavioral logical lines (non-blank, non-comment) MUST be
  ≤ 500. Overlay-authored logical lines MUST be ≤ 150. Violation rejects.
- **R4.4** **Referential integrity.** Every room id, prop instance id, prop id,
  card id, task id, buff id, dialog node id, and effect id referenced by the
  artifact MUST resolve against live world content. Unknown references reject;
  they are never silently dropped. This mirrors the strictness of the loaders in
  `server/content/worlds.py`.
- **R4.5** **Additive only.** The artifact MUST NOT redefine, wrap,
  monkey-patch, or shadow the authored module. It MUST NOT import anything
  outside a small allowlist (a stdlib subset plus `server.behaviors.*` and
  `server.content.*`). Violation rejects.
- **R4.6** **Smoke test.** The artifact MUST import in a restricted harness and
  MUST expose only the expected handler names — `on_tick`, `on_quick_action`,
  `on_card_play`, `on_dialog_action`, `on_activity_result`. Import failure or an
  unexpected public API rejects.
- **R4.7** Rejection reasons MUST be structured and specific — which rule,
  which line, which reference — and MUST be retained with the job row.

### R5 — Runtime overlay

- **R5.1** The runtime MUST load the authored floor and the committed overlay as
  two distinct modules, dispatching to both, with the authored module invoked
  first.
- **R5.2** An overlay failure MUST be contained to the overlay. The existing
  containment in `BehaviorDispatcher._dispatch` (`dispatcher.py:261-264`) MUST
  extend to overlay modules such that an erroring overlay is disabled for the
  remainder of that version's life while the floor continues to serve.
- **R5.3** Both modules MUST share the same `BehaviorContext` and the same
  `world.behavior_state` row for the peep (`namespace="peep"`,
  `instance_id=<peep_id>`), so state written by either is visible to both
  within a dispatch.
- **R5.4** Committing a new version MUST hot-swap the loaded module without
  restarting the world and without interrupting an in-flight dispatch. The swap
  MUST be atomic with respect to the dispatcher.
- **R5.5** The previous 3 committed versions MUST remain loadable for
  **operator-initiated** rollback. Rollback is never automatic.
- **R5.6** Because v1 peeps are room-bound, the overlay MUST NOT need to resolve
  a new room, and the room attachment map built at
  `server/behaviors/loader.py:125-134` remains valid. This invariant MUST be
  asserted by a test.
- **R5.7** Overlay-written behavior state MUST be version-tagged so a new
  version can migrate or reset it deliberately rather than blindly reading
  another version's keys.
- **R5.8** A dynamic peep with **no committed overlay** MUST behave exactly as
  today — authored floor only. Absence of generation MUST be indistinguishable
  from the feature being off, apart from a log line.

### R6 — Dialog memory

- **R6.1** Dialog generation MUST be append-only. The agent MAY add nodes; it
  MUST NOT modify, reorder, or remove any authored node, nor alter any authored
  choice's `label`, `next`, `action`, `script`, `give_card`, `start_task`, or
  `grant`.
- **R6.2** Every generated node id MUST carry a `dynamic_` prefix — the
  machine-checkable marker that also matches the existing unreachable-node
  escape hatch in `server/content/worlds.py:471-481`.
- **R6.3** `action_id` is synthesized as `f"{node_id}:{index}"`
  (`worlds.py:430`) and is the `reward_ledger` key, so generated node ids MUST be
  **cycle-scoped** (`dynamic_<peep>_<version>_<slug>`). A generated node MUST NOT
  reuse an authored node id, and no two cycles may collide. This guarantees no
  reward is ever re-issued or permanently voided.
- **R6.4** The combined authored + generated tree MUST be re-validated through
  the **existing** loader rules — start node present, `next` targets exist, no
  dangling edges. Authored nodes remain exempt from the reachability check by
  existing convention.
- **R6.5** Any generated `when` clause MUST use the same `StatusCondition`
  vocabulary as authored nodes (`server/content/conditions.py`).
- **R6.6** A generated choice MAY use `grant` and `give_card`, but its
  `action_id` MUST be stable across reloads of the same version so ledger
  idempotency holds.
- **R6.7** Validation MUST reuse `_load_dialog` rather than a parallel
  implementation. Divergence between two validators is a defect.
- **R6.8** Personalization — acknowledging a specific user, referencing a past
  interaction — MUST be driven by `behavior_state` and the digest, never by
  mutating authored text.
- **R6.9** A generated node that no authored choice leads to MUST still be
  reachable, via a generated choice on a reachable node.

### R7 — Configuration

- **R7.1** All configuration arrives via `TRSERVER_*` environment variables
  parsed in `server/config.py`, following the existing pattern. No new
  configuration file format.
- **R7.2** The minimum required set is enumerated in [§7](#7-configuration).
- **R7.3** The feature MUST be **off by default** and MUST appear in the README
  configuration table and in the dev-feature warning in `AGENTS.md`.
- **R7.4** The worker MUST refuse to start without complete model configuration
  and MUST fail loudly rather than silently no-op.

### R8 — Observability

- **R8.1** Every job MUST emit a structured JSON log line following the
  `server/mc_client.py:_log` convention, with event, peep id, version, window,
  outcome, and reason.
- **R8.2** Job state, artifact versions, and rejection reasons MUST be
  inspectable by operators — via a command or table consistent with the
  existing `.admin audit` and MC `/api/mc/*` surfaces.
- **R8.3** Cost and token accounting MUST be recorded per job so per-peep spend
  is attributable.
- **R8.4** A generation-cycle health metric MUST exist: success rate, rejection
  rate by rule, mean and p95 generation latency, and artifact size
  distribution. Per `doc/performance.md`, worker model cost is **excluded** from
  the game-loop perf tiers, but artifact import time **is** included in the
  `server` tier because it touches the dispatcher.

### R9 — Safety posture

See [§9](#9-safety-posture) for the full statement. Summary: v1 executes
agent-generated Python in-process and is accepted only under a dev-only flag
with mandatory guardrails and a blocking v1.1 follow-up.

### R10 — Testing

- **R10.1** The validator MUST have unit tests covering every rejection rule,
  each with a minimal passing and failing fixture. No model required.
- **R10.2** The overlay runtime MUST have tests for authored-only operation,
  overlay dispatch order, shared state, overlay error containment, hot-swap
  during a dispatch, and rollback.
- **R10.3** Observation capture MUST have tests asserting no change to existing
  dispatch or transaction behavior — the current `tests/test_milestone3_behaviors.py`
  and `tests/test_milestone3_dialogs.py` suites MUST pass unchanged.
- **R10.4** End-to-end must be testable with a **deterministic fake model**: a
  fixture returning canned artifacts — one valid, one oversized, one with a
  dangling prop reference, one with a non-additive dialog edit. The full cycle
  MUST run offline in CI.
- **R10.5** Dialog append-only rules MUST have tests proving an authored
  `action_id` can never be re-issued or voided by generation.
- **R10.6** A static check mirroring the 1200-line rule MUST enforce the 500/150
  budgets in-repo and MUST be added to the pre-commit checklist.
- **R10.7** Browser coverage MUST include at least one visual test that a
  generated dialog node renders and its choice is clickable, and one
  **baseline-preservation** test that a peep with no overlay renders identically
  to its existing baseline. The second is mandatory.
- **R10.8** `doc/db.md` MUST be updated to the new schema versions, correcting
  the existing drift (the doc says profile 6 / world 10; the code is 7 / 12).

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Components

| Component | Location (proposed) | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PeepObserver` | `server/behaviors/observer.py` | Hooks the dispatch path; appends observations within the intent transaction |
| `DigestBuilder` | `server/services/peep_digests.py` | Rolls observations into bounded per-window digests |
| `PeepRetention` | `server/services/peep_digests.py` | Batched pruning of raw observations |
| `AgentScheduler` | `server/services/peep_scheduler.py` | Cadence timers on game-time boundaries; enqueues jobs; never calls the model |
| `AgentJobStore` | `server/state/peep_jobs.py` | Job rows: enqueue, lease, heartbeat, terminal transitions, cost accounting |
| `BehaviorStore` | `server/state/peep_artifacts.py` | Versioned artifact metadata and active-version tracking |
| `ArtifactValidator` | `server/behaviors/agent/validate.py` | The R4 checks, as a pure function |
| `ModelClient` | `server/agent/model_client.py` | Outbound HTTPS, mirroring `server/mc_client.py` conventions |
| `PromptBuilder` | `server/agent/prompts.py` | Assembles artifact + digest + world constraints into the request |
| `AgentWorker` (separate process) | `tools/peep_agent.py`, `server/agent/` | Leases jobs, calls the model, validates, commits |
| `OverlayRuntime` | `server/behaviors/overlay.py` | Loads, unloads, and swaps overlay modules alongside the authored floor |
| `DynamicDialogMerger` | `server/services/dialogs.py` | Composes authored + generated nodes; reuses `_load_dialog` validation |

### 4.2 Data model

Four new tables in the **world** DB, added as world schema migration v13. The
profile DB is untouched.

```sql
-- Append-only raw signal. Pruned on a rolling window (R2.4).
CREATE TABLE peep_observations (
    id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    peep_id          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    behavior_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    room_id          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    event_type       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    action           TEXT,
    actor_kind       TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- user | npc | system
    actor_id         TEXT,               -- account_id or npc peep_id
    detail_json      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(detail_json)),
    occurred_at      TEXT    NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_peep_observations_peep_time ON peep_observations(peep_id, occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_peep_observations_peep_version ON peep_observations(peep_id, behavior_version);

-- The only observation input the agent receives (R2.1).
CREATE TABLE peep_digests (
    peep_id          TEXT NOT NULL,
    window_start     TEXT NOT NULL,
    behavior_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload_json     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (json_valid(payload_json)),
    observation_count INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (peep_id, window_start)
);

-- Versioned artifact history. Source lives on disk; this is metadata.
CREATE TABLE peep_artifacts (
    peep_id     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    version     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    source_path TEXT    NOT NULL,
    logical_lines INTEGER NOT NULL,
    checksum    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    status      TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- active | superseded | rolled_back | rejected
    rejection_reason_json TEXT CHECK (rejection_reason_json IS NULL
                                      OR json_valid(rejection_reason_json)),
    created_at  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    superseded_at TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (peep_id, version)
);

-- The generation queue. The unique key enforces R3.4 at the schema level.
CREATE TABLE peep_jobs (
    job_id        TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,
    peep_id       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    window_start  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    state         TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- pending | leased | succeeded | rejected | skipped | failed
    lease_expires_at TEXT,
    attempts      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cost_json     TEXT CHECK (cost_json IS NULL OR json_valid(cost_json)),
    reason        TEXT,
    created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (peep_id, window_start)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_peep_jobs_state ON peep_jobs(state, lease_expires_at);
```

`world_meta` (`key`/`value`) is suitable for lightweight scalars such as last
successful run per cadence, but MUST NOT hold artifact history — versioning
needs real rows with status transitions.

### 4.3 Artifact storage on disk

```
.local/peep-overlays/
  molly/
    v1.py
    v2.py
    v3.py
```

One immutable file per version. `BehaviorStore.commit` writes the file, then
inserts the metadata row; the reverse order is never taken. Files are
gitignored with the rest of `.local/`. Every artifact is retained on disk after
a rejected or erroring version so it can be inspected post hoc (R9.1).

### 4.4 Key API surface

Kept narrow and individually testable:

```
PeepObserver.record(event, context, behavior_version)         # R1, called from BehaviorDispatcher._apply
DigestBuilder.build(peep_id, window) -> dict                 # R2
PeepRetention.prune(now)                                     # R2.4/2.5
AgentScheduler.tick(now)                                     # R3.1 cadence boundary
AgentJobStore.enqueue(peep_id, window) -> job_id             # R3.4
AgentJobStore.lease(n) / heartbeat(job_id) / complete(job_id, state, reason, cost)
ArtifactValidator.validate(artifact_source, world, peep) -> ValidationReport   # R4, pure
BehaviorStore.commit(peep_id, source) -> version
BehaviorStore.activate(peep_id, version) / rollback(peep_id, version)
OverlayRuntime.mount(peep_id, version) / unload(peep_id)
```

**No client protocol changes.** Dynamic peeps are indistinguishable to the
browser beyond their new dialog choices and reaction text.

### 4.5 Flow — generation cycle

```
cadence boundary (game-day or hour, via server/game_time.py)
  └─> AgentScheduler.tick(now)
        for each dynamic peep whose window is closed and under cap:
          AgentJobStore.enqueue(peep_id, window_start)   # idempotent; UNIQUE (peep_id, window_start)
        commit

AgentWorker (separate process, own event loop)
  └─> lease job (expiry-bounded, heartbeat during the model call)
        ├─> BehaviorStore.load_active(peep_id)                 # previous version
        ├─> DigestBuilder.build(peep_id, window)               # bounded, deterministic
        ├─> ModelClient.generate(previous, digest, constraints)
        │     └─ failure ─> job = failed; previous version stays live
        ├─> ArtifactValidator.validate(...)                    # PURE, R4
        │     └─ failure ─> job = rejected(reason); artifact retained; previous stays live
        ├─> DynamicDialogMerger.compose(peep_id, generated_nodes)   # reuses _load_dialog
        │     └─ failure ─> job = rejected; previous stays live
        └─> BehaviorStore.commit(peep_id, source) -> version
              job = succeeded; cost recorded
              [out of band] world server observes the new active version and hot-swaps
```

### 4.6 Flow — runtime

```
game event (quick_action | dialog_action | card_play | enter | leave)
  └─> BehaviorDispatcher.dispatch(event)              # existing routing, unchanged
        ├─> attachment resolution                      # loader.py room map, still valid (room-bound)
        ├─> PeepObserver.record(...)                   # R1, same transaction as intents
        └─> _dispatch:  authored handler   (floor, first)
                       overlay handler    (versioned, second; failures contained per R5.2)
                           └─> intents ──> one hub transaction ──> broadcast
```

### 4.7 Hot-swap

The world server detects an active-version change at the same cadence it
already uses for tick environment expiry, or via the process-local notification
path used by hot-reload (`server/app.py:262-283`). The swap must not interleave
with an in-flight dispatch; the existing global `asyncio.Lock` in
`BehaviorDispatcher.dispatch` (`dispatcher.py:219-226`) is the natural
serialization point.

One subtlety to settle during implementation: `BehaviorLoader` derives
`script_id` as `behavior:<sha1(path)>` (`loader.py:62`). A new version whose
content is byte-identical to an old one will therefore resolve to the same
`script_id` and the module cache will reuse the older module. Decide
explicitly whether that is the desired no-op behavior, and cover it with a test
rather than leaving it to chance.

---

## 5. Failure modes and degradation

| Failure | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Model endpoint down or timeout | Job `failed`; prior artifact stays live; peeps behave as static. Exponential backoff, capped attempts, then abandon the window |
| Model returns unparseable output | Job `failed` as a parse error. No retry beyond the attempt cap |
| Artifact fails validation | Job `rejected` with a specific reason. Artifact written to disk for inspection. Prior version live |
| Artifact valid but errors at runtime | Overlay disabled for that version's life; floor continues; surfaced in R8.2 |
| Generated dialog breaks the tree | Merged-tree validation fails ⇒ the whole cycle is rejected. Commit is atomic, never partially applied |
| Worker process down | Leases expire; jobs reclaimed by the next worker. No gameplay impact |
| Feature flag off | World server path is identical to today. The worker refuses to start |
| Cost cap hit mid-cycle | Job `skipped` with a reason. No partial artifact |
| Clock jump or DST | Cadence uses `game_time.today_in` and game-date semantics, never naive elapsed time |

**Absolute invariant: no generation failure may ever degrade gameplay.** The
worst case is a static peep.

---

## 6. Runtime constraints carried into the design

These are properties of the current codebase that the design must respect.
They are not defects introduced by this milestone.

- **Rooms with no connected humans do not tick** (`ticker.py:79`). For
  room-bound v1 this is acceptable — a peep with no observers has nothing to
  react to — but it MUST be documented as a limitation and re-examined when
  mobility lands.
- **`_account_for` resolves a target account** (`dispatcher.py:211-217`), so an
  overlay reacting to a user-initiated event already has full access to
  counters, buffs, cards, and grants against that user. No dispatcher change is
  required for the v1 reaction surface.
- **`activity_result` is never dispatched today.** The bridge in
  `server/routes/activity_bridge.py:17-44` completes activities without emitting
  the event, even though the dispatcher supports the type
  (`dispatcher.py:139-144`). This is the one event-source gap in scope.
- **Line-budget pressure.** Overlay code must stay well under the 1200-line
  rule and must not push `dispatcher.py` (629 lines) or `app.py` over it.
  Splitting `dispatcher.py` may be a prerequisite.
- **Doc drift.** `doc/db.md:12-13` and `:241` still state
  `PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 6` and `WORLD_SCHEMA_VERSION = 10`; the code is at 7
  and 12. Correct this in the same change that adds v13 (R10.8).
- **Unrelated drift.** `AGENTS.md` documents `server/client/` and `tests/client/`,
  which do not exist. The client-logic-testing convention in the agent guide is
  currently unsatisfiable.

---

## 7. Configuration

All variables are parsed in `server/config.py` following the existing pattern.
The feature is **off by default**.

| Variable | Required? | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TRSERVER_FEATURES` | Yes | _(none)_ | Must include `dynamic_peeps` to enable the feature and the worker |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_ENDPOINT` | Yes\* | — | Base URL of the model API |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_MODEL` | Yes\* | — | Model identifier |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_API_KEY` | Yes\* | — | Provider credential; environment only, never persisted |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_CA_FILE` | No | _(none)_ | PEM CA bundle for a private model endpoint |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_INSECURE_TLS` | No | `0` | Dev-only: skip model endpoint certificate verification |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_MAX_CALLS_PER_PEEP_DAY` | No | `2` | Per-peep call cap per game-day (R3.7) |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_PEEP_DAY` | No | `40000` | Per-peep token cap per game-day (R3.7) |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY` | No | `50` | Global daily call ceiling across all peeps |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_DAY` | No | `1000000` | Global daily token ceiling |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | No | `60` | Per-cycle wall-clock budget (R3.6) |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | No | `3` | Job attempts before abandoning the window |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_LEASE_SECONDS` | No | `300` | Job lease duration (R3.5) |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_OVERLAY_PATH` | No | `.local/peep-overlays` | Artifact root |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_OBSERVATION_RETENTION_DAYS` | No | `7` | Raw observation retention (R2.4) |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_DIGEST_RETENTION_DAYS` | No | `30` | Digest retention (R2.4) |
| `TRSERVER_PEEP_AGENT_VERSIONS_RETAINED` | No | `3` | Roll-backable versions per peep (R5.5) |

\* Required when `dynamic_peeps` is enabled. The worker refuses to start
without them (R7.4).

Per-peep cadence is authored in content, not in the environment:

```yaml
molly:
  label: Molly
  room: playroom
  script: molly.py
  dynamic:
    cadence: daily          # daily (default) | hourly
```

## 8. Testing strategy

| Layer | Location | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validator unit tests | `tests/test_peep_artifacts.py` | Every R4 rule with minimal passing and failing fixtures; no model, no network |
| Observation capture | `tests/test_peep_observations.py` | R1 schema and bounds; existing milestone-3 suites pass unchanged (R10.3) |
| Digest and retention | `tests/test_peep_digests.py` | Determinism, bounds, `per_user` threshold, pruning |
| Job store and scheduler | `tests/test_peep_jobs.py` | Idempotency, lease expiry and reclaim, cap enforcement, terminal states |
| Overlay runtime | `tests/test_peep_overlay.py` | Dispatch order, shared state, error containment, hot-swap mid-dispatch, rollback, room-bound invariant (R5.6) |
| Dialog merge | `tests/test_peep_dialogs.py` | Append-only enforcement; an authored `action_id` can never be re-issued or voided (R10.5) |
| End-to-end, offline | `tests/test_peep_agent.py` | Full cycle against a deterministic fake model returning four canned artifacts — valid, oversized, dangling prop reference, non-additive dialog edit (R10.4) |
| Static budget check | `tests/test_ui_presentation.py` or a sibling | Mirrors the 1200-line rule for the 500/150 budgets (R10.6) |
| Browser flow | `tests/browser/flows.spec.js` | A generated dialog node renders and its choice is clickable |
| Browser visual | `tests/browser/screenshots.spec.js` | Baseline preservation for a peep with no overlay (R10.7) |

The fake model is a **prerequisite**, not an afterthought: no end-to-end test
may touch the network.

---

## 9. Safety posture

> [!WARNING]
> v1 executes agent-generated Python in the game server process. This is
> accepted **only** under a dev-only feature flag and is **not safe for
> production deployment**.

### 9.1 Mandatory guardrails for v1

- The flag name MUST clearly denote untrusted execution and MUST be documented as
  never-for-production.
- The artifact import path MUST be distinct from the world-content import path,
  so the differing trust assumptions are visible in the code even though the
  mechanism is currently identical.
- Every artifact MUST be retained on disk for post-hoc inspection after a
  rejected or erroring version.
- The README MUST carry an explicit warning.

### 9.2 Blocking v1.1 hardening gate

Before any non-dev deployment, one of the following MUST be done:

1. **AST-level import and attribute allowlisting** over the generated artifact,
   replacing the R4.5 import-list check with real inspection of the parsed tree;
   or
2. **Migration to a declarative IR** — the agent emits a structured
   behavior spec (goals, schedule, reactions, dialog fragments) executed by a
   hand-written interpreter, so generated content can never execute code. This
   also converts the 500-line budget into a simple size cap.

This gate is a **blocking follow-up**, tracked in this document rather than in
informal notes. It is the reason the feature ships behind a flag.

### 9.3 Content integrity

- The runtime MUST NOT let an artifact modify `peeps.yaml` or any world content
  file. World YAML stays the source of truth for labels, images, rooms, props,
  and cards.
- No artifact may grant kudos or cards without a `ledger_key`. Unkeyed grants
  are already non-idempotent (`progression.py:245-253`); generated code is held
  to the stricter standard.

---

## 10. Complexity assessment and sequencing

**Overall: high.** For the locked scope — trusted Python, room-bound,
additive-only dialog, out-of-process worker — the estimate is **3–4 weeks** of
focused work for one experienced developer, with a clearly separable second
phase for the v1 debt in §9.2.

| Area | Share | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observation capture, digest, retention, migrations | ~20% | Individually cheap; the schema is a long-term commitment. Includes the `activity_result` gap |
| Job store, scheduler, leases, game-time cadence | ~15% | Straightforward once the day/hour boundary is settled |
| Model client, prompt assembly, cost accounting | ~15% | The prompt contract is the real design work, not the HTTP |
| Validator | ~15% | R4.4 referential integrity mirrors `server/content/worlds.py` and needs real care |
| Overlay runtime, hot-swap, rollback | ~20% | The trickiest correctness surface |
| Dialog append-only merge | ~10% | Mostly constrained by R6; a matter of reusing the existing validator correctly |
| Tests, static checks, docs | ~15% | Overlaps the above; the fake model is a prerequisite |

### 10.1 What is genuinely hard

1. **Hot-swap without interrupting a dispatch.** Everything else is CRUD. This
   needs a real argument about the dispatcher's global lock, module identity,
   and the `behavior:<sha1(path)>` `script_id` derivation described in §4.7.
2. **The prompt / validation contract.** Getting a model to produce artifacts
   that pass a strict validator *and* are actually interesting is an iteration
   problem, not a one-shot design. Expect several rounds against a corpus of
   real digests.
3. **Making "remembers this specific user" actually work** through the existing
   `reward_ledger`-keyed dialog system without a re-issue or a void. R6.3's
   cycle-scoped node ids are the crux.

### 10.2 Recommended sequencing

1. Observation capture + digest + retention + migrations + **fake model** +
   validator — all offline, zero runtime risk. Proves the data contract.
2. Overlay runtime + hot-swap + rollback, still with no model involvement.
3. Cadence scheduler + job store + real model client.
4. Dialog append-only merge.
5. Operator surface, metrics, docs, browser baselines.

Steps 1–2 carry the schedule risk and have no model dependency, which is exactly
the right order.

---

## 11. Non-goals for v1

- NPC movement and NPC position persistence
- NPC-to-NPC dialog
- Generated content in `rooms.yaml`, `cards.yaml`, or `props.yaml`
- Artifact sandboxing beyond the R4.5 import allowlist
- Generated quests or tasks
- Multi-agent deliberation
- World editor support for generated content

---

## 12. Open items

Resolved during specification, listed here for traceability:

1. **Artifact file layout** — separate immutable file per version
   (`.local/peep-overlays/<peep_id>/v<version>.py`). Cost: a small
   `BehaviorLoader` change so one peep can have two attachments.
2. **Cadence default** — `daily`, with `hourly` as an explicit per-peep opt-in
   in `peeps.yaml`. Tunable after real digests exist.
3. **Cost ceiling** — fixed conservative defaults (2 calls / 40k tokens per
   peep per game-day, plus global ceilings), overridable via `TRSERVER_*`.

Still open, and needing a decision before implementation of the affected area:

4. **Should generated dialog be visible in the world editor?** If yes, editor
   work is in scope. If no, generated content stays server-only and the editor
   needs an explicit "this tree differs from disk" warning so an author does not
   unknowingly discard it.
5. **Should digest building run on the game server or the worker?** Digest
   building reads the world DB and is cheap, so the game server is defensible,
   but it places AI-adjacent work on the gameplay process. Leaning worker-side,
   with the scheduler writing a closed-window marker the worker polls.
6. **Model provider and endpoint shape.** §7 assumes a generic OpenAI-style
   chat-completions surface. A different provider changes `ModelClient` and the
   cost-accounting fields but no other component.
